claims.note: Illustrative timeout arithmetic: a 26 s queued request against a 30 s client timeout, using the measured 26.2 s worst case; the client timeout is the reader-side assumption, not a measured value.
Derived from the measured cells: with one slot and a 3.2-3.3 s single request, the Nth queued request inherits N-1 waits, so a fixed client timeout bounds how many sessions can share a slot.
The context-multiply rule (2K with 4 parallel requests becomes 8K plus memory allocation) and the RAM scaling statement are quoted from the Ollama FAQ.

The /api/ps response recorded at 2026-11-02T08:10:30Z reported context_length 2048 for a server started with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4 and OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=2048; the multiply rule that makes that field an understatement is the FAQ rule.

run.methodology: one non-streaming POST /api/generate (num_ctx=2048, num_predict=8) against the OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4 server on 127.0.0.1:11435, immediately followed by GET /api/ps, 2026-11-02T08:10:30Z; the recorded context_length and size fields are the server-reported values for a model loaded with four slots configured.
